+  # Methods which are provided by StimulusReflex itself but are still safe to be
+  # invoked from the client. Every other method that is not explicitly defined by
+  # the developer on their own Reflex class (or one of its ancestors below

+  ALWAYS_CALLABLE_REFLEX_METHODS = [:default_reflex].freeze

@@ -8,15 +14,35 @@
   end
 
   private
 
+  # Only methods explicitly defined by the developer on the Reflex class - or on
+  # one of its ancestors, up to but *not* including StimulusReflex::Reflex - may
+  # be invoked from the client.
+  #
+  # Without this restriction, any public method inherited from Object/Kernel
+  # (`instance_variable_set`, `send`, `instance_eval`, `system`, `pry`,
+  # `remote_byebug`, ...) as well as internal Reflex methods (`render_collection`,
+  # ...) would be remotely callable, which allows for arbitrary code execution.
+  def callable_reflex_methods(reflex_class)
+    (reflex_class.public_instance_methods - StimulusReflex::Reflex.public_instance_methods + ALWAYS_CALLABLE_REFLEX_METHODS)
+      .uniq
+      .map(&:to_s)
+  end
+
+  def callable_reflex_method?(reflex)
+    callable_reflex_methods(reflex.class).include?(reflex.method_name.to_s)
+  end
+

-    method = reflex.method reflex.method_name

+
+    unless callable_reflex_method?(reflex)
+      raise NoMethodError.new("Reflex method '#{method_name}' is not callable on #{reflex.class.name}")
+    end
+
+    method = reflex.method method_name
     required_params = method.parameters.select { |(kind, _)| kind == :req }
     optional_params = method.parameters.select { |(kind, _)| kind == :opt }

-      reflex.public_send(reflex.method_name, *arguments)
+      reflex.public_send(method_name, *arguments)
     else

+++ b/lib/turbo_boost/commands/command.rb
@@
   class Command
     class << self
+      # Returns the list of public instance methods that are safe to invoke as commands.
+      #
+      # Only methods explicitly declared on Command subclasses (or on modules mixed into
+      # those subclasses) are considered safe. Methods inherited from
+      # `TurboBoost::Commands::Command`, `Object`, `Kernel`, `BasicObject`, etc.
+      # are NEVER invokable.
+      def command_methods
+        ancestors
+          .take_while { |ancestor| ancestor != TurboBoost::Commands::Command }
+          .flat_map { |ancestor| ancestor.public_instance_methods false }
+          .map(&:to_s)
+          .uniq
+          .sort
+      end
+
+      # Indicates if the passed method name is safe to invoke as a command
+      def command_method?(name)
+        name = name.to_s
+        return false if name.empty?
+        return false if name.start_with?("_") # internal/framework methods
+        return false unless name.match?(/\A[a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9_]*[?!=]?\z/) # no operators, no `send`-able tricks
+        return false if name.end_with?("=") # no writers
+
+        command_methods.include?(name)
+      end
+
+      # Indicates if the passed class name resolves to a Command subclass
+      def command_class?(klass)
+        klass.is_a?(Class) && klass < TurboBoost::Commands::Command
+      end
     end
--- a/lib/turbo_boost/commands/runner.rb
+++ b/lib/turbo_boost/commands/runner.rb
@@

-      unless command_class < TurboBoost::Commands::Command

           "Invalid command `#{command_name}`! `#{command_class_name}` is not a subclass of `TurboBoost::Commands::Command`."
       end
 
-      unless command_instance.respond_to?(command_method_name)
+      # NOTE: Do NOT rely on `respond_to?` or `public_methods` here.
+      # Those checks also match methods inherited from `TurboBoost::Commands::Command`,
+      # `Object`, `Kernel`, etc. and would permit unwanted code execution.
+      unless command_class.command_method?(command_method_name)

@@

-      @command_class ||= command_class_name.constantize
+      @command_class ||= begin
+        # Only resolve constants that look like a class name (prevents constant lookup abuse)
+        return nil unless command_class_name.match?(/\A[A-Z][a-zA-Z0-9_]*(::[A-Z][a-zA-Z0-9_]*)*\z/)

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+# Licensed to the Apache Software Foundation (ASF) under one

+# Unless required by applicable law or agreed to in writing,
+# software distributed under the License is distributed on an
+# "AS IS" BASIS, WITHOUT WARRANTIES OR CONDITIONS OF ANY
+# KIND, either express or implied.  See the License for the
+# specific language governing permissions and limitations
+# under the License.
+
+"""
+Read-Only SQL Validation Utilities
+
+Centralized and strict validation used to enforce the server read-only mode.
+Every SQL execution path must go through :func:`enforce_read_only` so that a
+client (even one holding a valid read-only account) cannot bypass the
+read-only restrictions, for example by:
+
+* prefixing a write statement with comments or optimizer hints
+  (``/* x */ DELETE FROM t``)
+* stacking several statements (``SELECT 1; DROP TABLE t``)
+* hiding a write operation inside a CTE / sub query
+  (``WITH c AS (SELECT 1) INSERT INTO t SELECT * FROM c``)
+* exporting data (``SELECT ... INTO OUTFILE``) or taking locks
+  (``SELECT ... FOR UPDATE``)
+"""
+
+import os
+import re
+from typing import Any, List
+
+
+class ReadOnlyViolationError(Exception):
+    """Raised when a SQL statement is not allowed in read-only mode."""
+
+    def __init__(self, message: str, sql: str = ""):
+        super().__init__(message)
+        self.message = message
+        self.sql = sql
+
+
+# Statement types that can never modify data or metadata
+_ALLOWED_STATEMENT_PREFIXES = (
+    "select",
+    "with",
+    "values",
+    "table",
+    "explain",
+    "describe",
+    "desc",
+    "show",
+    "help",
+    "use",
+)
+
+# Pure metadata lookups: they cannot contain nested statements, therefore the
+# deep keyword inspection below is not applied to them (so that legitimate
+# statements such as ``SHOW CREATE TABLE t`` keep working).
+_METADATA_STATEMENT_PREFIXES = ("show", "describe", "desc", "help", "use")
+
+# Write / administrative operations which must never appear anywhere inside a
+# statement executed in read-only mode.
+_FORBIDDEN_PATTERNS = (
+    r"insert",
+    r"upsert",
+    r"update",
+    r"delete",
+    r"drop",
+    r"alter",
+    r"create",
+    r"rename",
+    r"grant",
+    r"revoke",
+    r"merge",
+    r"load",
+    r"export",
+    r"import",
+    r"install",
+    r"uninstall",
+    r"kill",
+    r"cancel",
+    r"admin",
+    r"recover",
+    r"backup",
+    r"restore",
+    r"outfile",
+    r"dumpfile",
+    r"truncate\s+table",
+    r"replace\s+into",
+    r"for\s+update",
+    r"lock\s+in\s+share\s+mode",
+)
+
+_FORBIDDEN_REGEX = re.compile(
+    r"(?<![\w$])(?:" + "|".join(_FORBIDDEN_PATTERNS) + r")(?![\w$])",
+    re.IGNORECASE,
+)
+
+# Comments, string literals and quoted identifiers. They are removed before
+# the keyword inspection so that keywords cannot be hidden inside them and so
+# that legitimate literals/identifiers do not trigger false positives.
+_COMMENT_AND_LITERAL_REGEX = re.compile(
+    r"""
+      (?P<block>/\*.*?\*/)                # /* ... */ comments and hints
+    | (?P<line>(?:--|\#)[^\n]*)           # -- and # line comments
+    | (?P<single>'(?:\\.|''|[^'])*')      # 'string literal'
+    | (?P<double>"(?:\\.|""|[^"])*")      # "string literal"
+    | (?P<backtick>`(?:``|[^`])*`)        # `quoted identifier`
+    """,
+    re.DOTALL | re.VERBOSE,
+)
+
+_READ_ONLY_CONFIG_ATTRIBUTES = (
+    "read_only_mode",
+    "read_only",
+    "readonly",
+    "enable_read_only",
+)
+
+_READ_ONLY_ENV_VARIABLES = (
+    "DORIS_READ_ONLY",
+    "DORIS_READONLY",
+    "DORIS_READ_ONLY_MODE",
+    "READ_ONLY",
+)
+
+
+def _sanitize(sql: str) -> str:
+    """Remove comments and quoted content from a SQL statement."""
+
+    def _replace(match: "re.Match") -> str:
+        if match.lastgroup in ("block", "line"):
+            return " "
+        # Keep a harmless placeholder for literals / quoted identifiers
+        return " '' " if match.lastgroup == "single" else " x "
+
+    return _COMMENT_AND_LITERAL_REGEX.sub(_replace, sql)
+
+
+def _split_statements(sanitized_sql: str) -> List[str]:
+    """Split a sanitized statement list, dropping empty statements."""
+    return [part.strip() for part in sanitized_sql.split(";") if part.strip()]
+
+
+def _parse_bool(value: Any) -> bool:
+    if isinstance(value, bool):
+        return value
+    if isinstance(value, (int, float)):
+        return bool(value)
+    if isinstance(value, str):
+        return value.strip().lower() in ("1", "true", "yes", "y", "on", "enabled")
+    return bool(value)
+
+
+def is_read_only_mode(config: Any = None) -> bool:
+    """Determine whether the server currently runs in read-only mode.
+
+    The flag is looked up on the configuration object first and then in the
+    environment.  If no explicit configuration is found the check fails
+    closed (read-only is assumed), so that a missing/renamed option can never
+    silently disable the protection.
+    """
+    holders = []
+    if config is not None:
+        holders.extend(
+            [
+                getattr(config, "security", None),
+                getattr(config, "database", None),
+                config,
+            ]
+        )
+
+    for holder in holders:
+        if holder is None:
+            continue
+        for attribute in _READ_ONLY_CONFIG_ATTRIBUTES:
+            value = getattr(holder, attribute, None)
+            if value is not None:
+                return _parse_bool(value)
+
+    for variable in _READ_ONLY_ENV_VARIABLES:
+        value = os.getenv(variable)
+        if value is not None:
+            return _parse_bool(value)
+
+    # Fail closed
+    return True
+
+
+def validate_read_only_sql(sql: str) -> str:
+    """Validate that ``sql`` is a single, purely read-only statement.
+
+    Raises:
+        ReadOnlyViolationError: if the statement is not allowed.
+    """
+    if not sql or not sql.strip():
+        raise ReadOnlyViolationError("Empty SQL statement is not allowed", sql)
+
+    sanitized = _sanitize(sql)
+    statements = _split_statements(sanitized)
+
+    if not statements:
+        raise ReadOnlyViolationError(
+            "SQL statement does not contain any executable command", sql
+        )
+
+    if len(statements) > 1:
+        raise ReadOnlyViolationError(
+            "Multiple SQL statements are not allowed in read-only mode", sql
+        )
+
+    statement = statements[0].lstrip("( \t\r\n")
+    keyword_match = re.match(r"[A-Za-z_]+", statement)
+    if not keyword_match:
+        raise ReadOnlyViolationError(
+            "Unable to determine the SQL statement type, execution rejected", sql
+        )
+
+    keyword = keyword_match.group(0).lower()
+    if keyword not in _ALLOWED_STATEMENT_PREFIXES:
+        raise ReadOnlyViolationError(
+            f"Operation '{keyword.upper()}' is not allowed in read-only mode", sql
+        )
+
+    if keyword not in _METADATA_STATEMENT_PREFIXES:
+        forbidden = _FORBIDDEN_REGEX.search(statement)
+        if forbidden:
+            operation = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", forbidden.group(0)).upper()
+            raise ReadOnlyViolationError(
+                f"Operation '{operation}' is not allowed in read-only mode", sql
+            )
+
+    return sql
+
+
+def enforce_read_only(sql: str, config: Any = None) -> str:
+    """Validate ``sql`` when the server is running in read-only mode."""
+    if is_read_only_mode(config):
+        validate_read_only_sql(sql)
+    return sql

+"""Validation of uploaded files.
+
+Uploaded files are served from the site's own domain. Files that contain
+active content (JavaScript in html, xhtml or svg documents) therefore are a
+potential stored XSS vulnerability. To avoid this, uploads are validated
+before they are accepted.
+
+A validator is a callable with the following signature::
+
+    def validator(file_name: str, file: typing.IO, owner, mime_type: str) -> None
+
+It has to raise ``FileValidationError`` if the file must not be uploaded.
+
+Validators are registered per mime type. Wildcard keys (``"text/*"`` or
+``"*/*"``) are supported. The default policy can be changed with the
+``FILER_ADD_FILE_VALIDATORS`` and ``FILER_REMOVE_FILE_VALIDATORS`` settings,
+e.g.::
+
+    FILER_ADD_FILE_VALIDATORS = {
+        "image/svg+xml": ["filer.validation.deny"],
+    }
+"""
+import html.parser
+import mimetypes
+import typing
+
+from django.conf import settings
+from django.core.exceptions import ValidationError
+from django.utils.module_loading import import_string
+from django.utils.translation import gettext_lazy as _
+
+
+class FileValidationError(ValidationError):
+    """Raised if an uploaded file does not pass validation. The upload is
+    rejected in this case."""
+
+
+def deny(file_name: str, file: typing.IO, owner, mime_type: str) -> None:
+    """Denies the upload of a file unconditionally."""
+    raise FileValidationError(
+        _('File "{file_name}": Upload denied by site security policy').format(
+            file_name=file_name
+        )
+    )
+
+
+def deny_html(file_name: str, file: typing.IO, owner, mime_type: str) -> None:
+    """Denies the upload of html-like documents since they may contain
+    arbitrary JavaScript. Superusers are trusted and may upload them."""
+    if owner is None or not getattr(owner, "is_superuser", False):
+        raise FileValidationError(
+            _('File "{file_name}": HTML upload denied by site security policy').format(
+                file_name=file_name
+            )
+        )
+
+
+class ScriptFinder(html.parser.HTMLParser):
+    """Searches (x)html/svg markup for active content: scriptable tags, event
+    handler attributes and script-like urls."""
+
+    DISALLOWED_TAGS = frozenset({
+        "script", "handler", "iframe", "frame", "embed", "object",
+        "foreignobject", "set", "animate",
+    })
+    URL_ATTRIBUTES = frozenset({
+        "href", "xlink:href", "src", "action", "data", "from", "to", "values",
+        "begin", "attributename",
+    })
+    DISALLOWED_URL_PREFIXES = (
+        "javascript:", "vbscript:", "livescript:", "data:text/html",
+        "data:application/xhtml", "data:image/svg",
+    )
+
+    def __init__(self):
+        super().__init__(convert_charrefs=True)
+        self.is_safe = True
+
+    def handle_starttag(self, tag, attrs):
+        if tag.lower() in self.DISALLOWED_TAGS:
+            self.is_safe = False
+            return
+        for attribute, value in attrs:
+            attribute = (attribute or "").lower()
+            if attribute.startswith("on"):
+                # Event handler, e.g. onload="alert(1)"
+                self.is_safe = False
+            elif attribute in self.URL_ATTRIBUTES and self._is_unsafe_url(value):
+                self.is_safe = False
+
+    # Self-closing tags, e.g. <script src="..."/>, need to be checked, too
+    handle_startendtag = handle_starttag
+
+    @classmethod
+    def _is_unsafe_url(cls, value: typing.Optional[str]) -> bool:
+        if not value:
+            return False
+        # Browsers ignore whitespace and NULL bytes when parsing url schemes
+        url = "".join(value.split()).replace("\x00", "").lower()
+        return url.startswith(cls.DISALLOWED_URL_PREFIXES)
+
+
+def validate_svg(file_name: str, file: typing.IO, owner, mime_type: str) -> None:
+    """SVG files are xml documents which browsers render like html. Reject
+    them if they contain any active content."""
+    content = file.read()
+    if isinstance(content, bytes):
+        content = content.decode("utf-8", errors="ignore")
+    parser = ScriptFinder()
+    parser.feed(content)
+    parser.close()
+    if not parser.is_safe:
+        raise FileValidationError(
+            _('File "{file_name}": Rejected due to potential cross site scripting '
+              'vulnerability').format(file_name=file_name)
+        )
+
+
+#: Default upload policy
+DEFAULT_VALIDATORS: typing.Dict[str, typing.List[typing.Callable]] = {
+    "text/html": [deny_html],
+    "application/xhtml+xml": [deny_html],
+    "image/svg+xml": [validate_svg],
+}
+
+#: Effective registry, built by :func:`configure_validators`
+validators: typing.Dict[str, typing.List[typing.Callable]] = {}

+_configured = False

+
+def _load(validator):

+    return import_string(validator) if isinstance(validator, str) else validator

+def _as_list(validator):
+    if callable(validator) or isinstance(validator, str):

+    return list(validator)
+

+    """(Re-)builds the validator registry from :data:`DEFAULT_VALIDATORS` and
+    the ``FILER_ADD_FILE_VALIDATORS`` / ``FILER_REMOVE_FILE_VALIDATORS``
+    settings."""
+    global validators, _configured
+
+    validators = {
+        mime_type: list(funcs) for mime_type, funcs in DEFAULT_VALIDATORS.items()
+    }
+    for mime_type, funcs in getattr(settings, "FILER_ADD_FILE_VALIDATORS", {}).items():
+        mime_type = mime_type.lower()
+        for func in _as_list(funcs):
+            func = _load(func)
+            if func not in validators.setdefault(mime_type, []):
+                validators[mime_type].append(func)
+    for mime_type, funcs in getattr(settings, "FILER_REMOVE_FILE_VALIDATORS", {}).items():
+        mime_type = mime_type.lower()
+        for func in _as_list(funcs):
+            func = _load(func)
+            if func in validators.get(mime_type, []):
+                validators[mime_type].remove(func)
+    _configured = True
+
+
+def get_validators(mime_type: str) -> typing.Iterator[typing.Callable]:
+    """Yields all validators registered for ``mime_type``."""
+    if not _configured:
+        configure_validators()
+    mime_type = (mime_type or "application/octet-stream").lower()
+    main_type = mime_type.split("/")[0]
+    for key in (mime_type, f"{main_type}/*", "*/*"):
+        yield from validators.get(key, [])

+    """Validates a file that is about to be uploaded. Raises
